description: Library to make fluid, declarative animations in React Native. Provides Animated.Value, Animated.ValueXY, timing, spring, decay, and composition functions.

valueTypes.description: For single value animations. Can bind to style or props, interpolated, and drives multiple properties.
For 2D vector animations such as pan gestures.

decay.description: Animates a value from an initial velocity to zero using decay.

timing.description: Animates a value along a timed easing curve.

spring.description: Animates a value using spring physics (damped harmonic oscillator).

methods.add: Creates new Animated value by adding two Animated values.
methods.subtract: Creates new Animated value by subtracting second from first.
methods.multiply: Creates new Animated value by multiplying two values.
methods.divide: Creates new Animated value by dividing first by second.
methods.modulo: Creates new Animated value as modulo of a value.
methods.diffClamp: Limits a value between min and max based on value difference.
methods.delay: Starts an animation after a given delay.
methods.sequence: Runs animations in order, waiting for each to complete before starting the next.
methods.parallel: Runs animations simultaneously. Can use stopTogether flag.
methods.stagger: Runs animations in sequence with a staggered delay.

loop.description: Loops an animation a specified number of times or infinitely.

event.description: Maps events (e.g., gestures, scroll) to animated values.

methods.forkEvent: Attach a new JS listener to an existing AnimatedEvent.
methods.unforkEvent: Remove a JS listener from an AnimatedEvent.
methods.start: Starts the animation. Optional callback provides {finished: boolean}.
methods.reset: Stops animation and resets value to original.

interpolation.description: Maps input ranges to output ranges. Supports extrapolation, clamping, and easing.

utility.createAnimatedComponent: Wraps any React component to make it animatable.
utility.attachNativeEvent: Imperative API to attach animated value to events. Prefer Animated.event with useNativeDriver.

notes: Do not modify animated values directly; use useRef or Animated.Value.
Use useNativeDriver: true to offload animation to native UI thread.
Animations can be composed using parallel, sequence, stagger, delay, loop.
